items.passage: Brakes shrieked somewhere under the floor, and the compartment smelled of wet wool and the oranges my father had been peeling since we left Krakow. He had my article open on his knee again. For the third time that morning he was translating it, line by line, for Tatiana, a woman with a cello case who had made the mistake of asking where we were going. His Polish turned my four modest paragraphs into something closer to a speech. I told him the piece was about drainage policy and that no one on earth needed to hear it twice. He nodded and kept going. I was not embarrassed, exactly; I had simply heard the paragraph about storm grates often enough to recite it. At Tarnów, Tatiana got off, and my father folded the page into careful quarters. When he dozed against the window, I took the spare copy from my own bag, smoothed its creases, and tucked it into the pocket of his coat, beneath his ticket.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her father's translating of her article?
options: Irritated by his repetition while putting up with it to keep peace on the train
Touched by his attention while mostly regretting that she chose so dull a subject
Quietly pleased by his public display while passing off her objections as weariness
Embarrassed by his public reading while hoping that Tatiana would leave the compartment soon
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 기사가 배수 정책에 관한 것이라며 두 번 들을 필요가 없다고 불평하지만, 중간의 'not embarrassed, exactly'라는 정정은 불평이 진짜 불쾌감이 아니라 지겨움인 척하는 말투임을 보여 준다. 뒤에서 화자는 아버지가 잠든 사이 여분의 기사를 펴서 그의 코트 주머니에 몰래 넣어 준다. 말투와 행동의 어긋남을 합치면 C처럼 겉으로는 지겨운 척하지만 속으로는 아버지의 자랑을 기뻐하는 태도가 된다. A는 말투만 읽은 해석이고, B는 애정의 이유를 화자 자신의 후회로 바꾸었으며, D는 화자가 정정한 'embarrassed'를 그대로 빌려 와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Oaxaca had been dry for weeks, and the gate of the community garden on Calle Murguía stayed padlocked past nine. Ximena waited with a sack of seedlings she had bought before she had anywhere to put them. A man in a straw hat, Emiliano, waited too. While they stood there he pointed out which beds belonged to whom, which faucet leaked, and which neighbor would lend a hoe if asked twice. He told her that the first month was the hardest and that the soil here forgave mistakes. On the fence beside them hung a tin sign with a plot number painted over in blue. Neither of them mentioned it. When the coordinator finally arrived, out of breath, she unlocked the gate and handed out two sets of keys. She asked Emiliano to sign the register under the heading for new members, just below the line where Ximena had written her name. He took off his hat to do it, then stood holding the pen a moment longer than the signature required.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It presents a newcomer gathering practical advice from a helpful stranger during a delay.
It depicts two new members signing a garden register after a coordinator arrives late.
It shows how a stranger's advice prompts a newcomer to sign up as a garden member.
It reveals that a stranger's assured guidance came from someone hardly less unfamiliar there.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Emiliano는 텃밭의 구획, 새는 수도꼭지, 이웃의 성향까지 알려 주며 경험 많은 주민처럼 행동한다. 뒷부분에서 그는 Ximena 바로 아래 신규 회원 칸에 서명하고 펜을 오래 쥐고 있어, 그 역시 막 시작하는 사람이었음이 드러난다. 두 사건을 연결하면 D처럼 자신 있는 안내가 사실은 거의 똑같이 낯선 사람에게서 나왔다는 아이러니가 요지가 된다. A는 사건 1만, B는 사건 2만 요약했고, C는 조언이 가입의 원인이라는 인과를 만들어 두 사건의 관계를 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: Steam and blueing and the slap of wet cotton on stone: that was the laundry on Grant Road, and that was where Mohan taught me to fold. A sari, he said, had to be halved, then halved again, the border kept outward so a customer could see the work at once. He made me do it forty times one afternoon, until the creases lay flat as pressed leaves. 'One day these shelves are yours,' he said, and went back to his ledger. On the top shelf, behind the starch tins, sat a letter with a Poona postmark that nobody opened while I was in the room. Two years later I told him about the teaching post in Poona. He did not answer. That evening I found my trunk on the counter, already filled, every blouse and sari halved and halved again, borders turned outward, and the lid left open for me to close.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It reveals that lessons meant to tie a girl to the shop also prepared her departure.
It describes a stepfather passing the careful skills of his trade to his stepdaughter.
It depicts a young woman telling her stepfather about a teaching post in Poona.
It suggests that a stepfather began his lessons once he learned of her plans to go.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Mohan은 사리를 접는 법을 가르치며 언젠가 이 선반이 화자의 것이 될 것이라고 말해, 접기 수업이 가게를 잇게 하려는 일로 보인다. 뒷부분에서 그는 화자가 떠난다고 하자 같은 방식으로 접은 옷으로 트렁크를 채워 두어, 그 기술이 떠날 준비에도 쓰이게 된다. 따라서 A처럼 머무르게 하려던 수업이 결국 떠남을 준비하게 했다는 관계가 요지다. B는 사건 1만, C는 사건 2만 다루며, D는 수업과 떠날 계획의 인과 방향을 뒤집었다.

items.passage: Three rules governed Miss Kai's shop on Harbour Street: measure twice, cut once, and walk the sea wall every Sunday after chapel. The first two I understood. The third she never explained. Each week in that summer of 1861 we went along the promenade at Kingston, she with her parasol, I a step behind with my hands still smelling of chalk, and each week she stopped at the same iron bench to watch the fishing boats come in. 'When you keep a shop of your own,' she said once, 'you will know why.' In her workroom lay a bolt of blue linen that she dusted but did not cut. Thirty years on, my own shop has a sign over the door and a boy who threads needles faster than I ever did. On Sundays he walks a step behind me. I stop at the iron bench. He has not yet asked why, and I have not yet decided what I would tell him.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: It records the rules an apprentice learned while working in a Kingston seamstress's shop.
It shows how a mentor's unexplained Sunday habit has passed into the narrator's own life.
It portrays a tailor who now trains a quick young apprentice in his own shop.
It suggests that the narrator's apprentice led him to recall his mentor's weekly walk.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 Kai가 설명하지 않은 세 번째 규칙, 즉 일요일마다 방파제를 걷고 같은 벤치에 멈추는 습관을 따라다닌다. 30년 뒤 화자는 자신의 견습생을 뒤에 두고 같은 벤치에 멈추며, 그 이유를 아직 설명하지 못한다. 두 시점이 반복 구조로 겹치므로 B처럼 스승의 설명 없는 습관이 화자 자신의 삶으로 이어졌다는 것이 요지다. A는 앞 시점만, C는 뒤 시점만 요약했고, D는 견습생이 회상을 불러왔다는 식으로 인과를 뒤집었다.

items.passage: Receipts curled from the printer every few minutes at the all-night pharmacy on Długa Street, and Valentina tore each one off without looking. A year earlier, on the night her brother Suhyun left for his posting, he had borrowed her grey scarf for the bus to the barracks. She had texted him about it twice in the first month, once with a photograph of the empty hook by her door, and then had stopped. Her mother still asked whether he had answered. At ten past three one February morning, the door chimed. Suhyun stood by the cough syrups in a coat too thin for the Baltic wind, the grey scarf wound twice around his throat. Its fringe had been knotted back where it frayed, and one end was darned in thread a shade too dark. He set a packet of lozenges on the counter and reached for his wallet. Valentina pushed the coins back across to him.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It recounts a sister's repeated efforts to recover a scarf her brother had borrowed.
It depicts a late-night meeting between a pharmacist and her brother back from service.
It reveals that an item a sister thought neglected had been carefully preserved by him.
It suggests that a sister's messages about a scarf led her brother to keep away.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Valentina는 오빠가 빌려 간 스카프를 돌려받지 못해 메시지를 보내고 빈 옷걸이 사진까지 보내, 스카프는 무심하게 잊힌 물건처럼 보인다. 뒷부분에서 Suhyun은 그 스카프를 두르고 나타나는데, 해진 술은 다시 묶여 있고 끝은 꿰매져 있어 오래 아껴 써 왔음이 드러난다. 두 시점을 합치면 C처럼 방치된 줄 알았던 물건이 실은 정성껏 간직되어 왔다는 반전이 요지다. A는 사건 1, B는 사건 2만 말하고, D는 메시지가 오빠를 멀어지게 했다는 인과를 덧붙여 관계를 잘못 세웠다.

items.passage: Somchai never turned off the kitchen light. Every night at eleven she filled a glass of water, set it on the oilcloth beside the bread tin, and left the bulb burning over the stove. When the landlady complained about the bill, Somchai said the fuse box in that corner tripped whenever the switch was touched, and that she would rather pay than climb a ladder in the dark. The landlady let it go. The light had first stayed on in March, two nights after Karim was brought home by a taxi driver who had found him at the Charles Helou bus station holding a folded map of the southern roads. That same week the map disappeared from its nail in the hall. At two in the morning, Karim's slippers shuffled down the corridor, paused at the bright doorway, and turned in. Somchai, awake in the next room, listened to a chair scrape and a glass set down.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Somchai most likely leave the kitchen light on each night?
options: To avoid the risk of resetting an unreliable fuse box in a dark corner
To draw Karim toward a settled room before he could head out to the street
To keep up a nightly routine of preparing the kitchen before she went to bed
To make amends for having let Karim leave the house unnoticed in March
items.explanation: Somchai는 퓨즈 상자 때문이라고 말하지만, 불을 켜 두기 시작한 시점은 Karim이 남쪽 길 지도를 들고 버스 터미널에서 발견된 직후이고, 같은 주에 복도의 지도도 사라졌다. 마지막에 Karim의 발소리가 밝은 문간에서 멈춰 부엌으로 들어가고, 물잔이 놓이는 소리가 들린다. 시점 단서와 끝 장면을 결합하면 B처럼 밤에 헤매는 Karim을 거리 대신 부엌으로 이끌려는 것이 동기다. A는 표면 명분, C는 습관만 설명하며, D는 죄책감이라는 다른 감정으로 지도가 사라진 순서를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Folding chairs clattered onto the deck as my mother counted them aloud, one for each table she had already drawn on the back of a calendar. Every year on my birthday, since I was six, Yuxuan had taken me out on this same barge on the Tamsui, bought two bowls of fish-ball soup, and let me lean over the rail. Now she wanted my wedding banquet here. 'The good restaurant halls are booked until spring,' she said, when I asked. 'This is simpler, Jiayi.' I believed her until I opened the tea tin in her kitchen to find the sugar. Under the lid lay a deposit slip from the barge company, stamped in ink gone brown, dated 1977, my name on the back. I was seven that year and had not yet met anyone I would marry. I put the lid back. On the day itself, my mother walked to the stern before the guests arrived and tied a strip of red cloth around the third rail post.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Yuxuan most likely insist on holding the banquet on the barge?
options: To work around the shortage of open restaurant halls before the spring
To continue the birthday outings she had shared with her daughter for years
To honor an arrangement she had made for her daughter during childhood
To avoid the cost of a formal hall that she feared she could not pay
items.explanation: Yuxuan은 식당 연회장이 봄까지 예약이 차 있다고 말하지만, 화자가 찾은 바지선 예약금 영수증은 화자가 일곱 살이던 1977년 날짜에 화자의 이름이 적혀 있다. 해마다 생일에 같은 바지선을 탄 습관과 이 오래된 영수증을 합치면, 결혼 계획이 생기기 훨씬 전에 딸을 위해 해 둔 약속을 지키려는 동기가 드러난다. 따라서 정답은 C다. A는 표면 명분, B는 습관만 설명하고 영수증의 시점을 설명하지 못하며, D는 비용에 대한 걱정이라는 다른 감정으로 영수증의 날짜를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Rain drums on the galvanized roof, and the lamp smells of coconut oil and scorched wick. Each night Roshane sits across from you and copies your pages into his ledger, the French on the left, your English on the right, his pen scratching long after you have gone to bed. You had expected him to arrive with objections; his own novels sold better than yours in Paris. When you ask why he has not gone back down to Port of Spain, Linton, he says the road below the cocoa estate is washed out. Perhaps it is. Yet the boy who brought his mule up the hill led it home on Tuesday, a full day before the first rain. And the publisher's letter, the one asking for forty pages to be cut, is no longer on the shelf where you left it. On Sunday morning you find his finished ledger beside your inkwell, every chapter intact, its spine tied with your own blue ribbon.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Roshane most likely remain at the cottage?
options: To wait until the washed-out road below the estate could be crossed again
To keep up his nightly practice of copying the pages as fast as he could
To make up for the sales in which his novels had outpaced the author's
To complete a full version of the book before any requested cuts were made
items.explanation: Roshane은 길이 물에 잠겨 내려갈 수 없다고 말하지만, 노새를 끌고 온 소년은 첫 비가 오기 하루 전에 이미 노새를 데리고 돌아가 그가 처음부터 머물 계획이었음을 보여 준다. 또 40쪽 삭제를 요구한 출판사 편지가 사라졌고, 마지막에 장 하나 빠지지 않은 번역 원장이 놓여 있다. 시점 단서와 끝의 사물을 합치면 D처럼 삭제 요구가 실행되기 전에 책 전체를 옮겨 두려는 것이 동기다. A는 표면 명분, B는 습관만 설명하며, C는 미안함이라는 다른 감정으로 노새가 먼저 돌아간 순서를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: We arrived at the Posillipo pool at seven, because Elisa said the salt water was flattest before the swim club came. My brother brought goggles. She confiscated them. Her method had four parts, which she listed like train stops: lie back, ears under, hands open, stop trying. Fishermen's sons had learned it on this coast before anyone sold inflatable rings, she said, and now the sons sold inflatable rings. My brother sank eleven times. 'Count, Giada,' Elisa told me, so I counted from the bench, where the tiles were warm and someone had left half a lemon ice. On the twelfth try he drifted for perhaps nine seconds, arms out, staring at the sky. Elisa did not clap. She waded over, slid one palm under the back of his head, held it there without lifting, and waited until the swim club's whistle had blown twice before she took her hand away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Dryly amused and quietly tender toward a fading coastal skill
Lighthearted and playful toward a boy's clumsy swimming lesson
Relieved and gentle toward a lesson that has finally ended
Nostalgic and fond toward the coastal villages of the past
items.explanation: 앞부분은 고글 압수, 기차역처럼 나열한 네 단계, 어부의 아들들이 이제 튜브를 판다는 대목처럼 건조하고 농담 섞인 서술로 겉 어조를 만든다. 끝에서 Elisa는 박수 대신 아이의 머리 밑에 손을 받친 채 호루라기가 두 번 울릴 때까지 기다려, 사라져 가는 기술과 배우는 아이를 조용히 아끼는 속 어조가 드러난다. 따라서 두 층을 함께 잡은 A가 정답이다. B는 겉 층만, C는 Elisa의 손길을 끝났다는 안도로 원인을 뒤집었고, D는 대상을 해안 마을 전체로 넓혔다.

items.passage: Wira takes his coffee black at the Tutuban station café, two sugars, at 5:40, before the first run to Cubao. I, Narong, take mine at the next table. Between sips he fixes things. Tuesday it was the cashier's transistor radio. Wednesday, a schoolboy's calculator, opened with a bent fork. Thursday the waitress brought her mother's wristwatch, and he wound it, listened, adjusted something with a pin, and handed it back ticking. Everyone says he should open a shop. Nobody says it while holding out money. On Friday his own watch was missing from his wrist, a pale stripe where the band had been, and he checked the time on the café clock instead. He finished his coffee, counted coins for it twice on the saucer, and walked out to the bus with the waitress's thanks still being called after him across the room.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Cheerful and admiring toward a driver's talent for small repairs
Plainspoken and quietly uneasy toward generosity that goes unrewarded
Gloomy and sympathetic toward a driver's loss of his own watch
Detached and critical toward a neighborhood that takes favors freely
items.explanation: 앞부분은 요일별로 고친 물건을 건조하게 나열해 감탄스러운 솜씨를 담담하게 기록하는 겉 어조를 만든다. 그러나 '누구도 돈을 내밀며 그 말을 하지는 않는다'는 문장과, 자기 시계가 없어 카페 시계를 보고 동전을 두 번 세는 끝 장면이 대가 없는 노동에 대한 조용한 불편함을 드러낸다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만, C는 속 어조의 원인을 시계 분실 자체로 돌렸고, D는 비판의 대상을 동네 전체로 넓혔다.

items.passage: We divided the house in an afternoon. Colby took the kitchen table, I took the barometer, and we flipped a coin for the ladder, which he won and then lent back to me before I reached the car. The harder item was the gate. Twelve summers ago we had rebuilt the cemetery gate at St. Elwyn's together, my welding and his hinges, or his welding and my hinges, depending on which of us was telling the vicar. The parish newsletter had printed his name alone. I had kept the clipping in the barometer's case, folded small. On the way out of the village we stopped at the gate. Colby ran a thumb along the top rail. I said the hinges still swung true. Before we left, I took the clipping from the case and wedged it into the post's old crack, name side out, where the rain off the headland could reach it.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Amused and lighthearted toward the chore of dividing a family home
Gracious and yielding toward a brother who lent back the ladder
Wry and quietly generous toward a long-standing dispute over credit
Nostalgic and fond toward the summers the brothers spent on the coast
items.explanation: 앞부분은 집을 오후 한나절에 나누고 동전으로 사다리를 정하는 등 가볍고 건조한 농담조로 진행된다. 하지만 화자는 Colby의 이름만 실린 기사를 오래 접어 간직해 왔고, 마지막에 그 기사를 이름이 보이게 대문 기둥에 끼워 두어 공로 다툼을 조용히 내려놓는다. 따라서 겉의 재치와 속의 너그러움을 함께 담은 C가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만, B는 양보의 원인을 사다리 일로 바꾸었으며, D는 대상을 해안의 여름 전체로 넓혔다.

items.passage: Gopal addressed her as Secretary inside the cooperative's shed at Balaramapuram, as everyone did, and she addressed him as the new clerk. In 1912 Colette's ledgers were the pride of the district; inspectors from Trivandrum said no weavers' society in Travancore balanced so neatly. In his third week Gopal found out why. Beside each month's shortfall, in pencil so faint it was nearly gone, was a small mark and a sum, and the same sums appeared, a day later, as withdrawals from her own post-office book, which she kept in the drawer with the stamps. He closed the drawer. At the month's end the looms of two widows again fell short of their dues. Colette sat with her spectacles and her pencil. Before she could reach the drawer, Gopal set a folded envelope on the ledger, the flap tucked in, and asked the Secretary whether the inspectors would come on Thursday or Friday.
items.question: Colette is Gopal's grandmother; based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between them?
options: A junior clerk who works respectfully under the cooperative's admired secretary
A newcomer who learns how the cooperative keeps records from a skilled officer
A grandson whose own shortfalls are privately covered by the grandmother he serves
A grandson who, beneath formal deference, takes on the burden his grandmother bore
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 사람은 'Secretary'와 '새 서기'라는 공적 호칭으로만 서로를 부른다. 중간에서 Gopal은 Colette가 부족한 회비를 자기 우체국 저금으로 몰래 메워 왔다는 것을 알게 되고, 끝에서 그녀가 서랍에 손을 뻗기 전에 봉투를 먼저 내려놓아 그 비용을 대신 치른다. 따라서 겉의 격식 아래에서 할머니의 짐을 손자가 떠맡는 D가 정답이다. A는 호칭이 말하는 공식 관계, B는 앞 장면만 반영한 관계이고, C는 비용을 치르는 방향을 뒤집었다.

items.passage: When the supply boat came on the first of each month, Linus climbed to the keeper's quarters at Kyōga Point with his father's letter in English and bowed in the doorway as if he had never been there before. Sakura called him Mr. Linus and read the letter aloud to her father in Japanese. In November the letter said that the arrears must be paid by December. Sakura read that the arrears could wait until the herring returned in spring. Linus, who had studied Japanese at the Maizuru school for six years, looked at the barometer on the wall. He said nothing. Her father poured tea for him and wrote the word for spring in the margin of his calendar. In December, a receipt arrived from the agent marked paid in full. Clipped to it was a refund stub for Linus's own New Year passage home.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Linus and Sakura?
options: Partners in a quiet evasion, with Linus bearing the cost of Sakura's version
A landlord's son and a tenant's daughter observing formal monthly courtesies
Acquaintances whose monthly visits have made them easy in each other's company
Partners in a quiet evasion, with Sakura shielding Linus from his father's demands
items.explanation: 앞부분의 절과 'Mr. Linus'라는 호칭은 지주의 아들과 세입자 딸이라는 격식 있는 관계를 보여 준다. 그러나 Sakura가 체납금 독촉을 봄까지 기다려 준다는 말로 바꿔 읽을 때 일본어를 아는 Linus는 침묵하고, 12월에는 그의 귀향 뱃삯 환불 영수증이 완납 영수증에 붙어 와 그가 비용을 치렀음이 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 호칭이 말하는 공식 관계, C는 앞 장면만 반영한 관계이며, D는 누가 누구를 보호하는지 방향을 뒤집었다.

items.passage: Why does she carry you up, if you walk to the well by yourself? Clement, the missionary's boy from the floor above, asked it from the landing in his careful Korean, and nobody on the stair answered. Each evening since the autumn of 1889 the daughter had come back from the market, set down her basket, bowed, and said, 'Mother, permit me,' before taking the old woman's arm for the climb. Each evening her mother permitted it. Neighbors had seen the old woman at the well at noon, hauling a full jar without stopping. They had also seen the daughter's own door, two streets away, shuttered since her husband's funeral, the key left with the potter. On the night of Clement's question, the mother glanced at the boy, then at her daughter's raw hands. On the third step she let her knee give a little and leaned her full weight onto her daughter's shoulder.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between the daughter and her mother?
options: A dutiful daughter who formally attends an aging and increasingly frail mother
A mother who accepts being tended in order to give her grieving daughter a role
A mother whose strength at the well makes her daughter's evening help unneeded
A daughter who shields her proud mother from the neighbors' remarks about her
items.explanation: 앞부분의 'Mother, permit me'와 절은 딸이 노쇠한 어머니를 격식 있게 모시는 관계처럼 보이게 한다. 그러나 어머니는 한낮에 혼자 물동이를 나를 만큼 건강하고, 딸의 집은 남편 장례 이후 닫혀 있으며, 끝에서 어머니는 아이의 질문 뒤 일부러 무릎을 꺾어 딸에게 몸을 기댄다. 이 양보 동작은 어머니가 상실을 겪은 딸에게 돌볼 대상을 남겨 주려 한다는 B의 관계를 보여 준다. A는 공식적 관계, C는 우물 장면만 반영한 관계이며, D는 보호의 방향을 뒤집었다.

items.passage: Glue and tar and old paper: that is what the workshop on Jalan Kembang Jepun smells like, and the tar comes from your rope. You carried it off Matteo's freighter four years ago, coiled around a bundle of clothes, when the captain found you behind the rice sacks and, instead of calling the harbor police, brought you here. In the workshop the rope is useful. You tie finished stacks of ledgers with it for delivery, then untie it and coil it again by your bench, always beside the cloth bundle you never quite unpack. Matteo, who binds books now instead of sailing, has stopped asking about the bundle. This year he taught you headbands, the small stitched cords at the top of a spine. On Friday you take the rope, unpick it strand by strand, and sew the strands into the headband of a ledger for the harbor office. Then you shake the bundle open, Putri, and fold your shirts into the drawer under the bench.
items.question: In the text, the rope most likely represents
options: a practical means of securing stacks of ledgers for delivery.
the risky voyage that brought Putri hidden aboard the freighter.
Putri's lasting readiness to move on, which she finally gives up.
Putri's strained bond with Matteo, which she finally sets right.
items.explanation: 밧줄은 처음에 원장 묶음을 묶는 도구로 등장하지만, 늘 풀지 않은 옷 보따리 옆에 감겨 있어 언제든 떠날 준비와 함께 놓인다. 마지막에 Putri는 밧줄을 풀어 책 머리띠로 꿰매 넣고, 이어서 보따리를 풀어 셔츠를 서랍에 정리한다. 두 맥락을 아우르면 밧줄은 C처럼 언제든 떠나려던 마음과 그것을 내려놓는 변화를 상징한다. A는 문자적 기능이고, B는 앞 맥락만 반영했으며, D는 Matteo와의 관계 회복으로 읽었지만 지문에 두 사람 사이의 갈등 단서는 없다.

items.passage: I worked the customs booth at the Haifa road checkpoint that spring, and I watched the red stakes come. Amit, the surveyor from the city, drove them himself, one every twenty meters, along the line on his blueprint, which crossed Avraham's orchard behind my booth. Avraham drove his crates past me each morning and did not look at them. In May a wind came off the bay and bent his youngest fig nearly to the ground. When I passed at noon, one of the red stakes had been pulled from the line and driven in beside the fig, the trunk bound to it with a strip of sacking. Amit saw it on his rounds. He stood a long time with his blueprint. Then he took a fresh stake from his truck, measured a meter past the fig's roots, hammered it in there, and erased something on the paper with the end of his pencil.
items.question: In the text, the red stakes most likely represent
options: markers that a surveyor uses to record a planned boundary line.
an outside authority dividing land against a farmer's wishes.
a rift between two men that a farmer's act of repair begins to heal.
an imposed division that both men quietly bend to protect what grows.
items.explanation: 붉은 말뚝은 처음에 도시에서 온 측량사가 과수원을 가로질러 박는 경계 표시로 등장한다. 중간에 Avraham은 말뚝 하나를 뽑아 쓰러지는 어린 무화과나무의 지지대로 쓰고, 마지막에 Amit은 새 말뚝을 나무뿌리 너머에 박고 도면을 고친다. 두 맥락을 아우르면 말뚝은 D처럼 바깥에서 그어진 경계를 두 사람이 자라는 것을 지키기 위해 조용히 구부리는 것을 상징한다. A는 문자적 기능, B는 앞 맥락만 반영한 해석이며, C는 두 사람 사이의 불화 회복으로 읽었지만 마지막 동작은 관계가 아니라 경계선을 옮기는 것이다.

items.passage: Nadeesha, Father Xiulan said, as if he had seen me the Sunday before rather than three years ago, and he pressed a hymnal into my hands because the hall at the Railway Hotel had more guests than chairs. For the first hour of the wedding breakfast in that June of 1913 the book was only a convenience: I fanned myself with it, balanced my teacup on it, set my gloves on its cover. We talked about the bride's lace, the rain, the price of a ticket to Dublin. We did not talk about the choir loft at St. Nicholas, where I had stood every Sunday until my brother's funeral. When the fiddlers paused, he leaned over, opened the hymnal to a page whose corner someone had long ago folded down, and went back to his cake. I closed it. Later, as the guests rose for the toast, I opened it again to the folded page and laid it face up on my chair.
items.question: In the text, the hymnal most likely represents
options: the narrator's tentative move back toward a subject the two leave unspoken.
a handy object the narrator uses to cool herself in the crowded hall.
the narrator's polite ease with social chatter at the wedding breakfast.
a quarrel between the narrator and the priest that she finally settles.
items.explanation: 찬송가집은 처음에 부채, 찻잔 받침, 장갑 받침으로 쓰이는 편리한 물건일 뿐이며, 두 사람은 화자가 오빠의 장례 이후 떠난 성가대 이야기를 피한다. 중간에 신부가 접힌 페이지를 펼쳐 주자 화자는 책을 덮지만, 마지막에는 스스로 그 페이지를 다시 펴서 의자 위에 펼쳐 둔다. 두 맥락을 아우르면 찬송가집은 A처럼 말하지 않는 주제, 즉 떠났던 신앙 생활 쪽으로 조심스럽게 돌아가는 움직임을 상징한다. B는 문자적 기능, C는 앞 맥락만 반영했고, D는 두 사람 사이의 다툼으로 읽었지만 지문에 다툼의 단서는 없다.

items.passage: Since his mother moved south to Bergen in October, Matheus had gone to the school music room every afternoon at three, before I, Tendai, could collect him. The recital it was meant for had been cancelled in November. He still practiced the same piece, the left-hand passage first, then the right, then both, and if I asked about Bergen he asked whether the car needed petrol. I sat on a radiator by the door and listened. Through December, in the hour before the polar dark became complete, he played __like someone clearing the same stretch of path while the snow fell faster than he could lift it__. On the last day before the holidays the music teacher left a new score on the stand, a duet, its second part marked for a parent. Matheus moved it to the side of the stand. He did not put it away.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase most nearly suggests that Matheus's playing
options: carried a heavy burden that grew as the winter darkness deepened.
made a scraping, laborious sound that filled the quiet music room.
was a steady effort to hold a routine as circumstances eroded it.
was a way of getting through the dark afternoons before going home.
items.explanation: 비유 앞에는 어머니가 떠나고 연주회가 취소된 상황, 그리고 아들이 같은 곡을 같은 순서로 매일 연습하며 어머니 이야기를 피하는 반복 행동이 놓여 있다. 같은 길을 계속 치우지만 눈이 더 빨리 쌓인다는 비유는 이런 맥락에서 무너지는 상황 속에서도 일상을 그대로 지키려는 꾸준한 노력을 뜻한다. 뒤에서 부모용 파트가 있는 이중주 악보를 치우지 않고 옆에 두는 디테일도 그가 변화를 완전히 밀어내지는 않음을 보여 주어 C와 맞는다. A는 무게, B는 소리라는 다른 속성에 기댄 해석이고, D는 문자적 의미로 범위를 넓혔다.

items.passage: Lugo had one clockmaker left, and his shop on Rúa Nova was where Carmela worked after school, which is how I, Declan, came to stand among forty ticking cases arguing with her about an essay handed in five minutes late. I had taken over her class in January, after the teacher she had had for six years retired without saying goodbye. Every time I said five minutes, Carmela reset one of the wall clocks, slid its hands back, and said they were all slow anyway. We went around like that for a quarter hour. Our argument was __a pendulum in a case built too narrow, knocking the same wood on each swing and never reaching the arc it wanted__. Behind the counter, her uncle opened the back of a mantel clock and blew dust from its works. When I left, Carmela had set every clock in the shop to the same minute, except one by the door, which she left alone.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined phrase most nearly suggests that the argument
options: was loud and repetitive, filling the shop with a steady noise.
had grown heavy and tiresome after a quarter hour of debate.
was confined to the shop where Carmela worked after school.
kept striking a small point while the larger grievance went unvoiced.
items.explanation: 비유 앞에는 화자가 6년간 Carmela를 가르친 선생님이 작별 인사 없이 은퇴한 뒤 반을 맡았다는 상황과, 화자가 '5분'을 말할 때마다 Carmela가 시계를 되돌리는 반복 행동이 있다. 너무 좁은 상자 속 진자가 같은 나무에 부딪히며 원하는 호를 그리지 못한다는 비유는, 다툼이 사소한 지각 문제에만 계속 부딪히고 진짜 불만에는 닿지 못한다는 뜻이다. 뒤에서 문 옆 시계 하나만 그대로 남겨 두는 디테일도 말하지 않은 무언가가 남아 있음을 암시해 D와 맞는다. A는 소리, B는 무게라는 다른 속성에 기댔고, C는 상자를 문자 그대로 가게로 읽었다.

items.passage:
Carbolic and rain on the benches,
a fan that ticks on every turn;
Wanjiru sits where the foremen sit,
her boots still red with the quarry's dust.
Across the room the new hire, Zhiming,
holds his cap the way he held the rope
before it slipped, before the crate came down
on the arm of the man behind the door.
Twice she has stood to speak to him.
Twice she has looked at the clock instead.
Her anger by now is __a stove banked for the night,
the coals still red beneath the ash,
no flame, but heat enough for morning__.
A nurse brings tea for both of them.
In Wanjiru's pocket the dismissal slip,
already signed, is folded twice,
and when the doctor calls the injured man's name
she rises, and she takes the boy along.
items.question: As used in the text, the underlined portion most nearly suggests that Wanjiru's anger
options: has subsided but been kept quietly alive rather than put out.
feels heavy and draining after the long hours of waiting.
gives off a warmth that has already turned into forgiveness.
is dangerous and likely to flare up at a small provocation.
items.explanation: 비유 앞에는 Zhiming의 실수로 동료가 다친 상황과, Wanjiru가 두 번 일어났다가 두 번 시계만 보는 망설임의 반복이 놓여 있다. 밤새 재 속에 묻어 둔 불씨가 불꽃은 없지만 아침까지 열을 지닌다는 비유는 분노가 가라앉았지만 꺼지지 않고 남아 있음을 뜻한다. 뒤에서 이미 서명한 해고 쪽지를 주머니에 간직한 채 소년을 데리고 의사에게 가는 디테일도 분노가 보류된 상태임을 보여 주어 A와 맞는다. B는 무게, D는 불꽃이 튀는 위험이라는 다른 속성에 기댔고, C는 열을 이미 용서로 넓혀 해고 쪽지를 설명하지 못한다.
